cards.meaning: Settings that change shell and/or script behavior
cards.notes: Turned on or off with set inside a script from the point you enable them.

cards.meaning: Enable an option by long name within a script
cards.notes: Takes effect from that point in the script onward (until disabled).

cards.meaning: Enable the same option with the short form
cards.notes: Equivalent to set -o option-name (e.g. set -v = set -o verbose).

cards.meaning: Disable an option within a script
cards.notes: Long and short forms match the enable forms.

cards.meaning: - turns the option on; + turns it off
cards.notes: Opposite of “plus = more.” Memory hook: - = on, + = off.

cards.meaning: Prints each command as the script reads it
cards.notes: Useful while learning; noisy in production. Disable with set +o verbose / set +v.

cards.meaning: Exit the script when a command fails
cards.notes: errexit is the long name that matches -e. Same option either way.

cards.meaning: Turn on errexit: first failed command ends the script; later lines do not run
cards.notes: In the notes’ exit_on_error.sh, cat fails and moving on is not printed.

cards.meaning: Do not exit on a failed command; script continues
cards.notes: Default Bash is +e (errexit off). cat still errors, but moving on is printed.

cards.front: set -e vs default after a failed cat
cards.meaning: With -e the script stops (no later echo). Default +e keeps going (later echo runs)
cards.notes: Memory hook: default Bash = keep going after a failed command. set -e = one failure ends the script. Compare the last line of the two outputs.

cards.meaning: Turn -e on for a sensitive block, then +e to return to default for the rest of the file
cards.notes: Options take effect from the set line; you can change them mid-script.
